title: Review an explicit checkout and add planted verdict fixtures
head: 7a16e4ec0d77d6fdb2a8692a659fd6e55f902b70
summary: PR #16 makes the reviewed checkout an explicit runPr input. Repository identity, relative review files, source cuts, behavior context and generated links follow that checkout while the downstream atlas, comparison, source-check and attention-policy implementations remain unchanged. Most of the added lines are planted regression fixtures, not new production behavior.
before: runPr discovers the repository through the process working directory. Relative steps and glossary paths are resolved there; a cwd argument is not part of its API.
after: runPr accepts cwd, defaulting to the process working directory. The selected checkout supplies Git context and relative input files, enabling one process to review different checkouts without changing its own working directory.

testEvidenceNotes: test/pr.test.mjs:269–274 is the new explicit-cwd regression. It uses an agent-supplied card and check:false, so it needs no provider/Jev call.
test/fixtures.test.mjs:24 invokes runPr with a separate worktree cwd, an agent-supplied card and recorded Jev answers. These are replay inputs, not live Jev judgments.
test/fixtures.test.mjs:12–14 skips TLC-dependent cases when required tooling is absent. Cases that are not skipped use actual configured model tooling; do not label skipped model cases as passes.
The existing test/behavior.test.mjs separately uses a fake statechart harness. Its parser/transformer coverage is not fresh formal verification.
scopeLimitations: This is a historical merged PR comparison at exact commits, not an open GitHub PR or a merge approval.
Only helper/pr.js changes in production. Five cached downstream capability descriptions have unchanged source files, but their selected-root/base assumptions still need integration evidence.
SPEC.md and three test/fixture paths are outside the production system map. They are explicit change-accounting gaps/assets, not silently ignored or all treated as production risk.
Source support is not execution evidence. No Jev request, provider call or model run was performed by this independent summary.
The original explicit-cwd test does not by itself establish repeated multi-checkout isolation, relative glossary behavior or all downstream contract compatibility.

The untrusted-checkout Git protections remain present in the selected-cwd Git call. The existing malicious-hook/fsmonitor test is useful regression evidence, while an explicit-cwd variant is a distinct targeted check.

captureRecommendation.name: Explicit checkout versus process checkout
captureRecommendation.method: Create separate controlled Git fixture repositories for the process context and requested target. Give each a unique origin, source text and agent-supplied card in the same relative steps filename. From the fixed process checkout, call the real base/head runPr exports with the target cwd, check:false and trustAtlas:false. Record caption, linked SHA/remote, source text, current process directory and missing-check findings.
captureRecommendation.expectedDifference: Base ignores the unknown cwd option and follows the process checkout; head follows the requested target. A second head call with another cwd should not inherit the first checkout context.
captureRecommendation.scope: Real runPr composition over controlled Git/source/card fixtures. This does not call a provider or live Jev, does not run untrusted model code and does not establish all repository behavior.
